mainTopic: הלל customs and the ברכה before it, the אגדה of the cup at the future feast, and the משנה of אפיקומן with שמואל's rule about מצה
overview: The גמרא finishes a teaching that says how הלל is said follows local מנהג. אביי limits this: only the ברכה after הלל depends on custom, because שמואל taught that every מצוה is blessed עובר לעשייתן, before doing it. Three פסוקים then show that עובר means 'ahead.' A ברייתא reports that רבי doubled verses in הלל. אביי explains that רבי אלעזר בן פרטא 'added' by doubling every verse from אודך onward. Next comes an אגדה: at the future feast for the צדיקים, the כוס של ברכה passes from אברהם to יצחק, יעקב, משה and יהושע. Each declines, until דוד accepts with 'כוס ישועות אשא.' A new משנה forbids ending the פסח meal with אפיקומן. רב, שמואל and רבי יוחנן define the word differently. שמואל also rules that nothing may follow the מצה, and the גמרא defends him from the משנה's wording. Finally, the גמרא begins a proposed proof for שמואל from a ברייתא about cakes, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How הלל is said depends on local custom
steps.stepSummary: The end of a quoted teaching: whether to double verses, say them once, or add a ברכה after הלל all follows the local מנהג.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they double, one doubles. Where they say it once, one says it once. Where they bless after it, one blesses. Everything follows the custom of the region.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a teaching (also found in the משנה in סוכה): the details of how הלל is recited follow the local custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three practices are listed: repeating certain verses, saying them only once, and saying a ברכה after הלל. The closing rule, הכל כמנהג המדינה, says that none of these is fixed. Each place follows its own custom. This is the base text that אביי will now narrow.

keyTerms.meaning: To double, meaning to repeat certain verses twice
To say 'simply,' meaning to say each verse only once
To say a ברכה after it (after הלל)
The custom of the region

phrases.english: [Where the custom is] to double, one doubles;
[where the custom is] to say it simply, one says it simply;
[where the custom is] to bless after it, one blesses;
everything is according to the custom of the region.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the base teaching on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doubling verses, saying them once, and a ברכה after הלל all depend on local מנהג.

steps.title: אביי limits the custom to the blessing after הלל
steps.stepSummary: אביי says only the ברכה after הלל depends on custom. The ברכה before הלל is a מצוה everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They only taught this about the blessing after it. But before it, it is a מצוה to bless.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains that 'follow the custom' applies only to the ברכה after הלל, not to the ברכה before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could read the teaching as saying that every ברכה on הלל is optional. אביי narrows it: the ברכה before הלל is required in every place. Only the closing ברכה changes from place to place.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They only taught…' — a formula that limits a rule
After it
Before it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברכה before הלל is a matter of custom. According to אביי, only the ברכה after it is.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
they taught [this] only regarding after it;
but before it, it is a מצוה to bless.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the base teaching in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה before הלל is obligatory everywhere. Only the ברכה after it follows custom.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for always saying a ברכה before הלל.

steps.title: שמואל's rule: bless before doing a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: אביי supports his view with שמואל's general rule that every מצוה is blessed עובר לעשייתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: For all מצוות, one blesses over them before doing them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source behind אביי's statement: a general rule that every מצוה gets a ברכה before it is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since every מצוה needs a ברכה beforehand, הלל cannot be different. So the ברכה before it is required. A ברכה afterward has no such general rule, which is why it can be left to custom.

keyTerms.meaning: Before doing them (literally 'passing ahead of their doing')
Blesses over them

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of עובר לעשייתן applies to all ברכות המצוות throughout הלכה.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
all the מצוות, one blesses over them
before their performance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for אביי's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that the ברכה before הלל is required
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's general rule that all מצוות are blessed עובר לעשייתן

steps.title: How do we know עובר means 'before'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for proof that the word עובר means 'ahead of' or 'before.'
steps.simpleTranslation: From where can we tell that this word עובר is a term for 'going before'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a word-meaning question. It sets up the next three steps, which each bring a פסוק as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עובר usually means 'passing.' It is not obvious that it means 'before.' The question asks for a source showing this usage.

keyTerms.meaning: What indicates? / From where is it understood?
A term meaning 'going first / preceding'

phrases.english: From where is it understood
that this word 'over'
is a term meaning 'preceding'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי עוֹבֵר לִישָּׁנָא דְּאַקְדּוֹמֵי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions a key word in שמואל's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that עובר means 'before.'

steps.title: Proof from אחימעץ overtaking the Kushite
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings the פסוק where אחימעץ 'passed' the Kushite, meaning he got ahead of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: As it is written, 'And אחימעץ ran by way of the plain and passed the Kushite.'
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer is a פסוק in which ויעבור clearly means getting ahead of someone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחימעץ outran the Kushite and got in front of him. So ויעבור here means 'went ahead of.' That shows the root עבר can mean 'before.'

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written
And he passed / overtook

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
as it is written:
'And Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain'
'and he passed the Kushite.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויעבור את הכושי shows that עבר means getting ahead.

steps.title: אביי's proof from יעקב passing before them
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a different פסוק: יעקב 'passed before them.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: From here — 'And he passed before them.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives another proof that עבר means going in front.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בראשית, יעקב went ahead of his family to meet עשו. Here the root עבר appears together with 'before them,' which makes the meaning of 'ahead' explicit.

keyTerms.meaning: From here (introduces another source)
Passed before them

phrases.english: Abaye said: from here:
'And he passed before them.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative source for the same point.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: והוא עבר לפניהם shows that עבר means going ahead.

steps.title: A third proof: their king passes before them
steps.stepSummary: Others cite the פסוק in מיכה: 'their king passes before them.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: from here — 'And their king shall pass before them, and ה׳ at their head.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third version of the proof, from נביאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king leading the people 'passes before them,' and ה׳ is 'at their head.' Both phrases describe being in front, so this confirms that עבר means 'ahead.'

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (an alternate version)
At their head

phrases.english: Some say: from here:
'And their king shall pass before them'
'and ה׳ at their head.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third alternative proof, closing this discussion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויעבור מלכם לפניהם shows that עבר means going first.
steps.whatToRemember: Every מצוה gets a ברכה עובר לעשייתן, before doing it. Three פסוקים show that עבר means 'ahead.'

steps.title: רבי doubled verses, רבי אלעזר בן פרטא added
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that רבי repeated certain words in הלל and that רבי אלעזר בן פרטא 'added' to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי doubles words in it. רבי אלעזר בן פרטא adds words to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of doubling in הלל and quotes a ברייתא about two תנאים' practices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the custom of doubling mentioned in step 1. רבי's practice is clear. But רבי אלעזר בן פרטא 'adding' words to הלל sounds strange, and that sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Doubles / repeats
Adds

phrases.english: It was taught:
Rebbi doubles words in it;
Rabbi Elazar ben Perata
adds words to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the doubling of הלל from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי repeated parts of הלל, and רבי אלעזר בן פרטא added to it.

steps.title: What did he add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'adding' to הלל means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'adds' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for clarification. It is setting up אביי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is unlikely that someone added his own new words to הלל. So the גמרא asks what this 'adding' really was.

keyTerms.meaning: What?

phrases.english: What does he add?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the term מוסיף in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of רבי אלעזר בן פרטא 'adding' to הלל.

steps.title: He added doubling from אודך onward
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the 'adding' was extra doubling: repeating every verse from אודך onward.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: He adds doubling from 'I will thank You' and onward.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that 'adding' means repeating more verses, not inventing new words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So both תנאים were doubling. רבי אלעזר בן פרטא extended the doubling to every verse from אודך כי עניתני to the end. This matches the custom of repeating those verses.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I will thank You' — the verse beginning אודך כי עניתני in הלל
Onward (literally 'downward')

phrases.english: Abaye said:
he adds doubling
from 'I will thank You' onward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מוסיף means doubling every verse from אודך onward.
steps.whatToRemember: The source for doubling verses from אודך onward in הלל is רבי אלעזר בן פרטא, as explained by אביי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the common custom of repeating the verses from אודך to the end of הלל.

steps.title: The future feast for the righteous
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא interprets ויגמל to mean that הקדוש ברוך הוא will make a feast for the צדיקים when He shows kindness to יצחק's descendants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוירא expounded, sometimes in the name of רב אמי and sometimes in the name of רב אסי: What is meant by 'And the child grew and was weaned'? In the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will make a feast for the צדיקים on the day He extends His kindness to יצחק's descendants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins an אגדה about a future feast. It is connected to the topic of the כוס של ברכה and הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ויגמל, 'was weaned,' is read as יגמול חסדו, 'He will bestow His kindness.' אברהם's feast for יצחק becomes a hint to a future feast for יצחק's children. The transmitter of the teaching is uncertain: רב אמי or רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Expounded
Sometimes
A feast for the righteous
That He will bestow His kindness

phrases.english: Rav Avira expounded,

phrases.aramaic: זִימְנִין אָמַר לֵיהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי
phrases.english: sometimes he said it in the name of Rav Ami

phrases.aramaic: וְזִימְנִין אָמַר לֵיהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: and sometimes he said it in the name of Rav Asi:
What is meant by what is written:
'And the child grew and was weaned'?
In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He,
will make a feast for the righteous
on the day He bestows His kindness
upon the descendants of Yitzchak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from הלכה about הלל to a related אגדה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ויגמל hints to a future feast for the צדיקים when ה׳ bestows kindness on יצחק's descendants.

steps.title: The cup of blessing is given to אברהם
steps.stepSummary: After the meal, the כוס של ברכה is first handed to אברהם אבינו to lead ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: After they eat and drink, they give אברהם our father the cup of blessing to recite the blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: the honor of leading the blessing is first offered to אברהם. This sets up the next part of the story, which continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם, the first of the אבות, is naturally given the honor first. The sentence ends mid-story, and his response comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The cup over which ברכת המזון is said
אברהם our father

phrases.english: After they eat and drink,
they give Avraham our father
the cup of blessing to recite the blessing,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the feast narrative begun in step 11.

steps.title: אברהם declines and passes the cup to יצחק
steps.stepSummary: אברהם אבינו refuses to lead ברכת המזון because ישמעאל came from him. He hands the cup to יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: אברהם says to them: I will not bless, because ישמעאל came from me. He says to יצחק: Take it and bless.
steps.whatsHappening: אברהם was offered the כוס של ברכה in the last step. Here he turns it down and passes it to his son יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being offered the cup is a great honor. אברהם feels unworthy because a wicked son, ישמעאל, came from him. This sets up a chain where each leader hands the cup to the next one.

keyTerms.meaning: I will not recite the blessing (I won't lead ברכת המזון)
אברהם's son through הגר, seen as wicked
Take (the cup) and bless

steps.confusionAlert: Each person's 'flaw' is not a sin they committed. It is a feeling of personal unworthiness. This is a humble refusal, not a punishment.

phrases.english: And he (Avraham) says to them: I will not bless,
because Yishmael came out from me.
He says to Yitzchak: Take and bless.
phrases.notes: "Take" means take the cup of blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹמֵר לָהֶן: אֵינִי מְבָרֵךְ, שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the feast story: אברהם responds to being handed the cup.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אברהם declines to lead ברכת המזון because ישמעאל descended from him, and he passes the cup to יצחק.

steps.title: יצחק declines and passes the cup to יעקב
steps.stepSummary: יצחק refuses because עשו came from him. He hands the cup to יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: יצחק says to them: I will not bless, because עשו came from me. He says to יעקב: Take it and bless.
steps.whatsHappening: The cup moves to יצחק. He also turns it down and passes it to his son יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same pattern as אברהם. יצחק feels unworthy because a wicked son, עשו, came from him.

keyTerms.meaning: יצחק's son, the wicked twin brother of יעקב

phrases.english: He (Yitzchak) says to them: I will not bless,
because Esav came out from me.
He says to Yaakov: Take and bless.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹמֵר לָהֶן: אֵינִי מְבָרֵךְ, שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנִּי עֵשָׂו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next link in the chain: יצחק receives the cup from אברהם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יצחק declines because עשו descended from him, and he passes the cup to יעקב.

steps.title: יעקב declines and passes the cup to משה
steps.stepSummary: יעקב refuses because he married two sisters while both were alive, something the תורה would later forbid. He hands the cup to משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: יעקב says to them: I will not bless, because I married two sisters while both were alive, and the תורה would later forbid them to me. He says to משה: Take it and bless.
steps.whatsHappening: יעקב turns down the cup and passes it to משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב's reason is different from the first two. It is not about a wicked child. It is about his marriage to רחל and לאה. At the time this was permitted, but the תורה later forbade it, so he feels it is a blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: Two sisters (רחל and לאה)
In their lifetimes, while both were alive
To forbid them (the איסור of אחות אשה)

steps.confusionAlert: יעקב did nothing forbidden. The תורה had not been given yet. The point is that the act would later be seen as an איסור.

phrases.english: He (Yaakov) says to them: I will not bless,
because I married two sisters in their lifetimes,
which the Torah would in the future forbid to me.
He says to Moshe: Take and bless.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹמֵר לָהֶם: אֵינִי מְבָרֵךְ, שֶׁנָּשָׂאתִי שְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת בְּחַיֵּיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next link: יעקב receives the cup from יצחק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יעקב declines because he married two sisters, a practice the תורה later forbade, and he passes the cup to משה.

steps.title: משה declines and passes the cup to יהושע
steps.stepSummary: משה refuses because he never entered ארץ ישראל, neither alive nor in burial. He hands the cup to יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה says to them: I will not bless, because I did not merit to enter ארץ ישראל, not in my life and not in my death. He says to יהושע: Take it and bless.
steps.whatsHappening: The cup moves past the אבות to משה. He turns it down and passes it to his student יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's flaw is a missed זכות, not a person or act. He was not even buried in ארץ ישראל, unlike יוסף, whose bones were brought there.

keyTerms.meaning: I did not merit
Neither in my life nor in my death (not even buried there)

phrases.english: He (Moshe) says to them: I will not bless,
because I did not merit to enter Eretz Yisrael,
neither in my life nor in my death.
He says to Yehoshua: Take and bless.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹמֵר לָהֶם: אֵינִי מְבָרֵךְ, שֶׁלֹּא זָכִיתִי לִיכָּנֵס לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next link: משה receives the cup from יעקב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה declines because he never entered ארץ ישראל, alive or dead, and he passes the cup to יהושע.

steps.title: יהושע declines because he had no son, with a verse as proof
steps.stepSummary: יהושע refuses because he had no son. A פסוק in דברי הימים lists the family line and stops at יהושע. He hands the cup to דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהושע says to them: I will not bless, because I did not merit a son. As it is written: 'יהושע son of נון,' and 'נון his son, יהושע his son.' He says to דוד: Take it and bless.
steps.whatsHappening: יהושע turns down the cup, and the גמרא brings a פסוק to show that he had no son. Then he passes the cup to דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the only refusal that comes with a proof from a פסוק. The family list of אפרים in דברי הימים ends with 'יהושע his son' and names no child after him. That shows he had no sons.

keyTerms.meaning: A son
As it is written (introduces a פסוק)
'נון his son.' From the family list of אפרים in דברי הימים א ז:כז, where the name נון is vocalized נוֹן

steps.confusionAlert: The first פסוק (במדבר) just names יהושע as the son of נון. The proof comes from the second פסוק, the family list that stops with יהושע.

phrases.english: He (Yehoshua) says to them: I will not bless,
because I did not merit a son,
as it is written: "Yehoshua son of Nun" (Bamidbar 14:6),
"Non his son, Yehoshua his son" (Divrei HaYamim I 7:27).
phrases.notes: The list ends here, with no son named after יהושע.

phrases.english: He says to David: Take and bless.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא זָכִיתִי לְבֵן, דִּכְתִיב: ״יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next link: יהושע receives the cup from משה. A scriptural proof is added inside the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהושע declines because he had no son, as the family list in דברי הימים shows, and he passes the cup to דוד.

steps.title: דוד accepts and leads the blessing
steps.stepSummary: דוד המלך accepts the cup and says it is fitting for him to bless, quoting 'כוס ישועות אשא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד says to them: I will bless, and it is fitting for me to bless, as it is said: 'I will lift up the cup of salvation, and I will call upon the name of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The chain of refusals ends. דוד takes the cup and leads ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone before דוד found a reason to decline. דוד is the one who accepts, and he grounds his claim in his own words in הלל (תהלים קט״ז). This links the story back to the הלל discussion earlier in the סוגיא.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is fitting for me to bless
I will lift up the cup of salvation (תהלים קט״ז:יג)

steps.whatToRemember: At the future feast, the honor of leading ברכת המזון passes from אברהם through יצחק, יעקב, משה and יהושע. Each one declines out of humility, until דוד accepts based on his פסוק in הלל.
steps.whyThisMatters: דוד, the author of הלל and the ancestor of משיח, closes the story. That fits the סדר theme of praising the גאולה over a cup of wine.

phrases.english: He (David) says to them: I will bless,
and it is fitting for me to bless,
as it is said: "I will lift up the cup of salvation
and I will call upon the name of ה׳" (Tehillim 116:13).

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹמֵר לָהֶן: אֲנִי אֲבָרֵךְ, וְלִי נָאֶה לְבָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the chain begun in step 12: the cup finally finds someone who accepts it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: דוד leads ברכת המזון at the feast of the צדיקים, based on 'כוס ישועות אשא'.

steps.title: New משנה: no אפיקומן after the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins: after eating the קרבן פסח, one does not finish the meal with אפיקומן.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One does not conclude after the פסח with אפיקומן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא's אגדה is over, and a new משנה starts. It sets a rule about how the פסח meal must end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids ending the פסח meal with something called אפיקומן, but it does not say what that word means. The גמרא will define it in the next steps. רב reads it as moving from one group to another, while שמואל and רבי יוחנן read it as extra foods eaten after the meal.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
One does not conclude or finish off (the meal)
A term the coming גמרא defines in different ways: moving to another group (רב), or extra foods after the meal (שמואל, רבי יוחנן)

steps.confusionAlert: In this משנה, 'אפיקומן' is NOT the piece of מצה we hide at the סדר. It means some extra thing added after the meal, and the משנה forbids it.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One does not conclude
after the Pesach (offering) with afikoman.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין מַפְטִירִין אַחַר הַפֶּסַח אֲפִיקוֹמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks from the אגדה and opens a new משנה with a new halachic topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After eating the קרבן פסח, one may not end the meal with אפיקומן.

steps.title: What does אפיקומן mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins and asks for the meaning of the unusual word אפיקומן from the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is אפיקומן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא section on the new משנה begins by asking what the strange word אפיקומן means. This question sets up a list of answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'אין מפטירין אחר הפסח אפיקומן' but never explained the word. The answer decides what exactly is forbidden after eating the קרבן פסח. Different meanings will lead to different rules.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
The word from the משנה whose meaning is being asked
What is?

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is 'afikoman'?
phrases.notes: The word looks Greek, which is why its meaning is unclear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה quoted in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definition of the word אפיקומן in the משנה.

steps.title: רב: do not move from one group to another
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that אפיקומן refers to not leaving one eating group to join another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It means that people should not get up and move from one group to another group.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer: the משנה is warning people not to leave their פסח group and go eat with another group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן פסח must be eaten by one registered group in one place. רב reads אפיקומן as related to 'take out the things,' meaning packing up and moving. So in רב's view, the rule is about place and group, not about food.

keyTerms.meaning: They will be uprooted, meaning they get up and leave
A group registered together to eat one קרבן פסח

phrases.english: Rav said: That they should not be uprooted (get up and leave)
from one group to another group.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: שֶׁלֹּא יֵעָקְרוּ מֵחֲבוּרָה לַחֲבוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אפיקומן means getting up and leaving one חבורה for another.

steps.title: שמואל: after-meal delicacies
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says אפיקומן means after-meal treats, giving examples of what he and רב liked to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: Things like mushrooms for me, and baby birds for אבא (רב).
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a second answer: אפיקומן means a dessert or treat eaten after the meal, like the mushrooms he liked and the young birds רב liked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the rule is about food, not about moving. After the קרבן פסח you may not add a fancy course that would cover its taste. 'אבא' here refers to רב, whose name was אבא אריכא.

keyTerms.meaning: Mushrooms
Young birds or chicks
Here, a name for רב (אבא אריכא)

steps.confusionAlert: 'לְאַבָּא' does not mean 'for my father.' It refers to רב, whose real name was אבא.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
Such as mushrooms for me,
and young birds for Abba (Rav).
phrases.notes: Each Amora names the treat he liked to eat after a meal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer from רב's, defining אפיקומן as food.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אפיקומן means after-meal delicacies such as mushrooms or young birds.

steps.title: רב חנינא בר שילא and רבי יוחנן: dates, roasted grain and nuts
steps.stepSummary: A third view says אפיקומן means snack foods like dates, roasted grain and nuts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חנינא בר שילא and רבי יוחנן said: Things like dates, roasted grain and nuts.
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer is given: אפיקומן means simple snack foods such as dates, roasted grain and nuts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view agrees with שמואל that the rule is about food. The difference is that it includes even plain snacks, not only fancy dishes. So the ban after the פסח is wider.

keyTerms.meaning: Dates
Roasted grain kernels
Nuts

phrases.english: And Rav Chanina bar Sheila
and Rabbi Yochanan said:
phrases.notes: The text is corrected from singular 'אמר' to plural 'אמרו' since two people are speaking.

phrases.english: Such as dates, roasted grain and nuts.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חֲנִינָא בַּר שֵׁילָא וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third definition, alongside רב and שמואל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אפיקומן means snacks like dates, roasted grain and nuts.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted that matches רבי יוחנן's definition word for word.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא like רבי יוחנן: One may not finish after the פסח with things like dates, roasted grain and nuts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבי יוחנן, giving his view support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the same language as the משנה ('אין מפטירין אחר הפסח') but fills in the examples: dates, roasted grain and nuts. This shows that a Tannaitic source understood the rule as being about these snack foods, exactly like רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
In agreement with him
Finish or conclude the meal (with more food)

phrases.english: It was taught in agreement with Rabbi Yochanan:
One may not finish after the Pesach
with things like dates, roasted grain and nuts.

steps.whatToRemember: There are three definitions of אפיקומן: רב (moving to another group), שמואל (fancy after-meal treats), and רבי יוחנן (snacks like dates and nuts). A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the view in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's definition of אפיקומן as dates, roasted grain and nuts.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that uses those same examples.

steps.title: שמואל: no אפיקומן after מצה either
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: even after eating מצה, one may not finish with אפיקומן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: One may not finish after מצה with אפיקומן.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule is stated: the ban on eating more food at the end applies not only after the קרבן פסח but also after the מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Today, with no קרבן פסח, the last thing eaten is מצה. שמואל rules that the same ban applies, so the taste of מצה stays in the mouth. This is a new law that goes beyond the words of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Unleavened bread eaten on the night of פסח

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for our practice of not eating anything after the final piece of מצה (the 'אפיקומן') at the סדר.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
One may not finish after matza with afikoman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining the word to extending the rule to מצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not eat אפיקומן foods after the מצה, just as after the פסח.

steps.title: Challenge: the משנה mentions only the פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: the משנה says 'after the פסח,' which implies after מצה it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: One may not finish after the פסח with אפיקומן. This implies: only after the פסח is it forbidden, but after מצה one may finish with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's rule by reading the משנה closely: since it only says 'after the פסח,' it seems that after מצה it would be allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a challenge from a precise reading of the wording (a דיוק). If the משנה named only the פסח, it suggests that מצה is different. That would contradict שמואל, who forbids אפיקומן after מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה
It is only this that is not allowed

phrases.english: We learned: One may not finish
after the Pesach with afikoman.
Only after the Pesach is it not allowed,
but after matza, one may finish (with afikoman)!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: אֵין מַפְטִירִין אַחַר הַפֶּסַח אֲפִיקוֹמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's rule in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that אפיקומן is forbidden after מצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה names only the פסח, implying that after מצה finishing with אפיקומן is allowed.

steps.title: Answer: 'needless to say' about מצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is teaching a bigger חידוש: of course after מצה it is forbidden; the surprise is that even after the strong-tasting פסח it is forbidden too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is speaking in a 'needless to say' style: Needless to say after מצה, whose taste is weak, it is forbidden. But after the פסח, whose taste is strong and can't easily be removed, you might think there is no problem. So the משנה teaches us that it is forbidden there too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the משנה chose the harder case (the פסח) to teach a bigger point, and the easier case (מצה) is obviously included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מצה has a weak taste, so any food afterward would wipe it out, so it clearly needs protection. The פסח meat has a strong taste that would stay anyway, so one might think extra food is fine. The משנה mentions the פסח to teach that even there it is forbidden, and שמואל's rule about מצה stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Needless to say; it is obvious
Its taste is strong
To remove it (the taste)
It teaches us

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the פסח is the 'stricter' case. It is actually the case where you would expect MORE leniency, because its strong taste stays anyway. That is why the משנה needed to state it.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule stands: nothing may be eaten after the final מצה. The משנה mentions the פסח only because that case was less obvious.

phrases.english: It is speaking in a 'needless to say' style:
Needless to say after matza,
whose taste is not strong (it is certainly forbidden),
but after the Pesach, whose taste is strong
and one cannot remove it,
(you might think) we have no problem with it; so it teaches us (that it is forbidden).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26 and defends שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the משנה as a 'לא מיבעיא' (needless to say) statement, so the inference is rejected.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פסח has a strong taste that stays, eating after it might be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even after the פסח it is forbidden, and after מצה it is certainly forbidden, so שמואל is correct.

steps.title: A proposed proof for שמואל from a ברייתא about cakes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a ברייתא supports שמואל. The ברייתא allows eating plenty of sweet cakes on פסח night, provided a כזית of מצה is eaten last.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say a source supports שמואל: sponge cakes, honey-oil cakes and honey cakes, a person may fill his stomach with them, as long as he eats a כזית of מצה at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to prove that שמואל is right. The ברייתא says you may fill up on sweet cakes, but you must eat a כזית of מצה last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said nothing may be eaten after the מצה. The ברייתא requires the מצה to come 'at the end', which sounds like the מצה must be the final taste of the night. If so, that fits שמואל's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say this supports him. It opens a proposed proof.
Soft sponge cakes
Cakes fried in oil and honey
Honey cakes
An olive-sized amount, the minimum for the מצוה of מצה

steps.confusionAlert: These cakes are kosher for פסח (no חמץ). The ברייתא is not about חמץ at all. It is only about the order of eating: cakes first, מצה last.

phrases.english: Let us say [this] supports him:
Sponge cakes, oil-and-honey cakes, and honey cakes,
a person may fill his stomach with them,
provided that he eats an olive-bulk of matza at the end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending שמואל from the משנה's wording, the גמרא now looks for positive support for him.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that nothing may be eaten after the מצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא requiring a כזית of מצה to be eaten 'at the end' after filling up on cakes

steps.title: Reading closely: matza at the end is good
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to read the ברייתא precisely: when the מצה is eaten at the end, yes, it is acceptable.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the end, yes, it works.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא focuses on the word 'at the end' in the ברייתא. This is a setup line: the גמרא is preparing to draw an inference from it in the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא clearly approves when the מצה comes last. The open question is what this implies about other orders of eating. The גמרא will spell that out next, and that is where the proof for שמואל will be tested.

keyTerms.meaning: At the end, eaten last
Yes. It marks what the source clearly allows.

phrases.english: At the end, yes,
phrases.notes: The inference continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins drawing a precise inference from the ברייתא quoted in the previous step.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The inference from the word 'בָּאַחֲרוֹנָה' in the ברייתא
